title: streaming-connection-resilience-and-context-handshake
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: implement a resilient streaming client in the Go SDK that cleanly interops with context cancellation and deadlines while minimizing spurious retries and preserving partial result semantics. This ticket covers runtime behavior, developer ergonomics, and concrete examples for application authors. We expect the new behavior to be backwards-compatible for simple use-cases but to expose richer controls (lease/heartbeat, retry tokens, and explicit close semantics) for advanced workloads.
acceptance_criteria: SDK cancelation: When a caller cancels ctx passed to NewStream or Read, the underlying RPC should be canceled promptly and any in-flight token accounting cleaned up (no goroutine leaks).

Deadline negotiation: If ctx has a deadline shorter than the server-side streaming lease, client should send an explicit 'client-deadline' header and honor the earlier deadline locally (no server-induced blocking beyond deadline).
Partial responses: Clients should surface partial messages received before cancellation through the stream API and make it explicit whether finalization occurred.
Retry behavior: Retries must be disabled if caller cancels; idempotency and resume tokens required to allow safe automatic retries for long-poll re-establishments.
Backpressure and buffering: Example shows how to apply a per-message read timeout vs overall stream deadline; SDK should provide helpers to combine them without losing deadlines.
No new test flakes: Unit and integration tests for cancellation races and deadline edge-cases pass reliably in CI across linux/amd64 and linux/arm64.
Documentation: README and godoc examples added demonstrating common cancellation patterns and graceful shutdown for servers and clients.
implementation_notes:
High-level approach:
1) StreamSession wrapper: implement a StreamSession type that owns a single RPC + a short-lived goroutine for reads. Expose ReadMsg(ctx) which accepts a per-call ctx to allow fine-grained timeouts.
2) Lease & header handshake: on stream open, send a client-side hint header 'X-RW-Client-Deadline' (unix-nanos) so server can prioritize or truncate long blocks; server still controls final termination.
3) Cancellation flow: when parent ctx Done fires, transition session to 'canceled' state, close read loop, cancel RPC context and emit a final ErrCanceled sentinel. Ensure we call cancel func exactly once to avoid races.
4) Retry/resume: introduce optional ResumeToken header for streams that can be resumed; token is provided by server in the last successful message. Automatic resume only when caller did not cancel and operation is idempotent.
5) Backpressure: use a small per-message buffer (size configurable) and expose SetReadBuffer / SetWriteBuffer to tune memory for high-throughput workloads.
6) Examples: provide two canonical examples: a) single-request streaming with overall deadline, b) long-lived subscription that uses heartbeats and per-message deadlines.

Trade-offs considered:
- Sending client deadline to server leaks local policy; acceptable because header is advisory and helps scheduling.
- Automatic resume vs explicit user control: we err on explicit control for non-idempotent streams.
design_decisions: Make per-message read function accept ctx rather than relying on the session-wide ctx; improves ergonomics for common patterns.
Server-provided resume token is optional; SDK will not attempt transparent resume unless ResumePolicy is set to 'auto' and user has not canceled context.
Do not multiplex different logical streams over a single RPC in this change; keeps cancellation semantics simple.
Expose debug metrics for cancelled-by-client vs cancelled-by-server for later UX and SLO analysis.
test_plan:
Unit tests: cancellation races around open/read/close, single-message partial-delivery, deadline header encoding/decoding.
Integration: local test server that simulates slow initial response, heartbeats and server-side forced pause. Reproduce a flaky situation from field bug where client with short deadline repeatedly leaked goroutines.
Load test: 10k concurrent streaming sessions with randomized deadlines to verify memory and goroutine bounds.
CI: Add a deterministic timing harness to reduce flakiness (use testClock in read loop).
rollout_plan:
1) Merge feature behind a Go SDK minor feature flag (env var RW_GO_STREAM_V2).
2) Dogfood internally with console telemetry pipelines and a small group of customers on Dedicated.
3) Monitor goroutine / lease metrics for 72h, rollback if goroutine growth detected.
4) Gradually remove feature flag in two weeks after stable signals.
updates: 2026-03-12: Ticket created. Initial design reviewed with runtime team; action: add explicit resume token flow.
2026-03-13: Implemented StreamSession skeleton and unit tests for basic cancel path. Found a race where cancel() could be called twice during reconnect - fixed with sync.Once.
2026-03-14: Added header encoding for X-RW-Client-Deadline and provisional examples for per-message ctx usage. Integration harness reproduces previous leak locally.
Next steps: finish resume-policy tests, add godoc examples, open PR for review.
comments: PM Review (Jordan Lee): 'Make sure the examples show both context.WithTimeout and a separate per-message timeout pattern; customers often mix them.'
Design Review (Sofia Martínez): 'Prefer explicit resume over auto-resume by default; we should surface a higher-level helper that composes resume tokens with idempotency checks.'
Security (Rahul Desai): 'No secrets in headers; the deadline header is advisory and permitted. Confirm we do not leak resume tokens to logs.'
Eng Note (Liam O'Connor): 'Working on buffering knobs and will add metrics for canceled_vs_server_terminated. Tracked under ENG-214672 for metrics dashboard.'
